dod_intent_evidence: News section: two AFWERX STTR Phase II awards of $1.8M each (July 2025 for AI-driven spatial analytics, November 2025 for signal fusion) with AFRL/AFWERX named, plus their own About page press item 'AIRIA Selected for US Air Force Grant to Enhance Sustainable Space Management & Safety for US Campuses & Bases' and a 'Federal' item in their site navigation.
score_evidence: 'Our self-learning software easily integrates with existing campus network data, leading to manageable fees, easy deployments & clear ROI' → lab_language_intensity (deployment framed as a commercial ROI event, not an accreditation event)

'Frictionless & Privacy Focused IT Integration ... Designed with robust cybersecurity in mind' — the only security language in ~1377 words, with zero mention of ATO, RMF, STIG, IL4/IL5, CMMC, NIST 800-171 or CUI despite two Air Force contracts → deployment_awareness_absence

'AIRIA provides campus facility operators real-time & 24/7 building occupancy data' — the only 'operators' in the pack are campus facilities staff; no airmen, security forces, defenders, CONOPS or field feedback anywhere → operator_absence
Sole open role: 'Software Engineer (C# / .NET / Python) — NYC (Hybrid)' — no field/deployment engineer, no ISSO, no compliance or security-engineering hire → hiring_profile_skew
'Seed round closed July 2025' + second STTR Phase II awarded 2025-11-24 at 13 employees → stage_pressure (two concurrent Phase II periods of performance against a 13-person team)

blind_spots.blind_spot: Treats network integration as a setup task rather than an accreditation event
blind_spots.operator_reality: On an Air Force installation the 'existing campus network' is an ATO'd DoD enclave. Getting a self-learning collector onto it means an RMF package, STIG'd hosts, a POA&M, and an ISSO signature — 9-18 months of work that has to start before the Phase II period of performance ends, not after. The Phase II money runs out while the package is still in review.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their entire delivered install base is university IT, where the CIO can just approve a collector; nobody in a 13-person team that has only ever shipped to campuses has carried an RMF package.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Seamless integration by leveraging existing IT infrastructure, reducing the time needed for installation and minimizing the risk of system disruptions.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Architecture assumes a continuous telemetry stream to a cloud analytics back end
blind_spots.operator_reality: 'Real-time & 24/7' occupancy inference off network telemetry dies the moment the site is on a DDIL segment, an austere or expeditionary location, or a network that blocks egress to a vendor cloud. Same failure mode as the crowd-detection startup that streamed 30fps into a link with bandwidth for one frame every five seconds — the fix is decoupling inference cadence from transport, and that is an architecture decision, not a config toggle.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Campus networks are fat, always-on, and permissively routed; there has never been a customer environment that punished the assumption.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: AIRIA provides campus facility operators real-time & 24/7 building occupancy data

blind_spots.blind_spot: Frames occupancy data as a privacy problem, not an OPSEC/CUI problem
blind_spots.operator_reality: Building-level occupancy and movement patterns on a military installation is pattern-of-life data — personnel density by facility and hour. On a base that is CUI at minimum and an OPSEC indicator at worst; it drives handling, storage location, aggregation limits and export controls, and a signal-fusion STTR compounds it. FERPA-shaped 'privacy protections' do not satisfy any of that.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The compliance model they built is the one universities audited them against; no one has yet told them the same dataset changes classification when the building is on an Air Force base.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Privacy as a Priority ... Built-in privacy protections. No hardware needed.

opener_hook: AIRIA has two AFWERX STTR Phase II awards inside 5 months ($1.8M each, July and November 2025), while airia20.com still describes the product as campus occupancy analytics that 'easily integrates with existing campus network data' — on an installation that integration is an RMF package and an ISSO signature, and the Phase II clock usually expires before the package clears.
what_they_do: AI spatial-analytics SaaS that infers building occupancy from existing network data to cut university facilities and energy costs, now pivoting the same engine toward Air Force signal fusion.
